title: Why cyclists and runners lean into a bend
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why do cyclists lean when they turn?

forces.label: Tyre grip to centre

explain.say: A moving body tends to keep going in a straight line. To curve round a bend, something must push you sideways towards the inside of the curve.

explain.say: On a bike or on your feet, that push comes from friction between the ground and your tyres or shoes. It points towards the centre of the bend.

explain.say: But that sideways push acts at the ground, below your body, so on its own it would tip you outwards. Leaning in lines up the ground's push with your centre of gravity, so you stay balanced.

explain.say: The faster you go or the tighter the bend, the bigger the push you need and the more you must lean. On ice, with little grip, the ground can't give that push and you slide straight on.

faq.q: Why do you lean when going round a bend?
faq.a: Leaning keeps you balanced. The road pushes you sideways towards the inside of the turn, at your wheels or feet. Tilting your body inward lines up that push with your centre of gravity, so it doesn't tip you over outwards.
asks: Why do cyclists lean on corners?

faq.q: What force turns you round a corner?
faq.a: Friction from the ground, pushing sideways towards the centre of the curve. Any inward push that keeps something moving in a circle is called a centripetal force; without it, you would carry straight on.

faq.q: Why do you feel thrown outwards on a bend?
faq.a: Your body tends to keep moving in a straight line, which is called inertia. When the bike or car turns, it pushes you round with it, but it feels as if you are being thrown outwards.
asks: Is there a force pushing you outward on a bend?

faq.q: Why do racetracks have sloped corners?
faq.a: Banked corners tilt the track, so the ground itself pushes partly towards the centre of the bend. Cyclists and cars can then turn fast without relying only on tyre grip.

faq.q: Why do you slide on an icy bend?
faq.a: Ice gives very little friction, so the ground can't supply the inward push you need to turn. Your body carries on in a straight line, and you slide off the curve.
asks: Why can't you turn on ice?

facts: An object keeps moving in a straight line at a steady speed unless a force acts on it: Newton's first law of motion.
Velodrome tracks are banked at up to about 45 degrees on the bends.

quiz.say: A cyclist turns a sharp bend on a dry road. What provides the force that turns them?
quiz.show: On a bend, the turning force comes from…

options.show: Friction between the tyres and the road
options.say: Friction between the tyres and the road

quiz.why: Tyre grip pushes the bike sideways towards the centre of the bend, which makes it curve instead of going straight.

wrong.1: Wind is not needed to turn; the bike turns just as well on a still day.
wrong.2: Weight pulls straight down, not towards the centre of the bend.
